assessments.reasoning: The first §4.2.5 paragraph at jls-4.2.5-100 identifies two primitive boolean values signaled by true and false. The earlier primitive types passage at jls-4.2-300 states the same cardinality.

challenge.method: Compared the first §4.2.5 paragraph with the numeric and reference comparisons in jls-4.2.5-200 and jls-4.2.5-210 and the null reference provision in jls-4.12.2-100. On Temurin 21.0.12.1+1 for Windows, evaluated a nonzero integer comparison and a null Boolean wrapper comparison. Separately compiled direct assignments of null and the integer 1 to primitive boolean with javac --release 21.
challenge.results: The comparisons yielded true and false, respectively. The compiler rejected both direct primitive assignments. A null Boolean is a reference value under §4.12.2.

limitations: The provision defines primitive boolean values at the Java language level. Boolean references belong to the reference type system.
